can someone explain me the differences between a haswell and a silvermont chip?thanks

Silvermont is the marketing name of Intels low power system on a chip (SOC) varients of Sandy Bridge with a focus on mobile, embedded, low cost systems. Hawell was their bleeding edge until Skylake replaced it. You've got to read up and be familiar with intels tick (minor) tock (major) to understand where everything fits in.

Tock (major) Sandy Bridge(32nm) Haswell(22nm) Skylake(14nm)
Tick(minor) Ivy Bridge(22nm) Broadwell(14nm) Kaby Lake & Cannonlake
SOC family Silvermont Silvermont Goldmont
Codename Silvermont(22nm) Silvermont(22nm) & Airmont(14nm) Goldmont
-- -- -- --
so in terms of power how powerful they can be even though they are low cost/consumption chips.thanks for your reply!

If youve ever used a cheap laptop (less than 400 dollars) from either AMD or Intel made in the last 2-3 years you'll have a good idea of just how powerful these products are. While these chips will be fine for light media consumption 99% of the time (video playback, web browsing) while not emptying the battery at the first sign of work but they are not the kind of things you'd play a game on or any heavy workloads on them.

They exist to fill the markets need for cheap laptops and help push the product range towards tablet / phone power envelopes (some are passively cooled) to try and keep ARM from dominating from the bottom up.
